subject: Executive recap: ClearFin leadership briefing, outcomes & escalation asks
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: John Lee <john.lee@clearfin.com>, Claire Dawson <claire.dawson@clearfin.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 15:14:00 -0700
Subject: Executive recap: ClearFin leadership briefing, outcomes & escalation asks

Hi John / Claire —

Thanks again for making time today. Below is a concise leadership-facing recap from our call with the ClearFin execs (John + Claire) and the technical/ops touchpoints we discussed. Purpose: align on business outcomes, capture the primary risks that will block procurement, and list ownership + requirements for the next 30 days.

High-level business outcomes (what ClearFin expects):
- Reduce fraud review time for manual cases by ~60% within pilot window (target: 2–3 weeks to surface false positives).
- 30% reduction in downstream chargeback volume during pilot-month due to improved inference precision.
- SLA: p95 latency under 350ms for the per-transaction scoring endpoint in production.

Key pain points discussed (validated):
1) Unpredictable latency spikes during high card-present volumes; current vendor has no regional routing.
2) Data residency / encryption requirements: production data must remain in their us-east VPC during pilot.
3) Auditability & model explainability: compliance needs a tokenized audit trail and a simple explanation surface per decision.

Top risks (blocking procurement or pilot start):
- Network egress / VPC setup timeline (ClearFin IT requires a security review + VPN termination).
- SOC2 evidence: legal wants a two-week turnaround on the SOC2 artifact and a KMS integration plan.
- Cost predictability: CFO needs an estimate for monthly committed spend if pilot scales beyond 500k requests.

Mutual Action Plan (30-day view) — owners & acceptance criteria:
- Redwood: Provide VPC architecture diagram + sample VPN termination playbook (owner: Rishi) — due: 2027-05-23.
- ClearFin: Share procurement checklist and PO template + legal primary contact (owner: Claire) — due: 2027-05-20.
- Redwood: Deliver SOC2 excerpt + KMS integration notes (owner: Priyom) — due: 2027-05-24.
- Joint: Pilot success criteria doc (latency, precision metrics, rollback plan) (owner: Soojin / Claire) — draft due: 2027-05-21.

Immediate asks / escalation items for ClearFin leadership to unblock timeline:
- Security review: assign a ClearFin IT lead who can do a 30–60 minute architecture sync with Rishi by 2027-05-19.
- Procurement: confirm if a one-month discovery PO is acceptable to start infra work while legal finalizes contract.

Attached: ClearFin_Risk_Table.xlsx (detailed risk matrix) and Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.pdf (draft MAP).

Next scheduled checkpoint: 2027-05-23 10:00am ET — VPC & Security sync (30 min). Please confirm or propose alternate time.

Thanks — we’ll move quickly on the deliverables above.

Best,

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0149

[Redwood Inference] Production-grade LLM inference — predictable, low-latency, and enterprise-ready
From: John Lee <john.lee@clearfin.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Dawson <claire.dawson@clearfin.com>, procurement@clearfin.com, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Executive recap: ClearFin leadership briefing, outcomes & escalation asks

Soojin —

Appreciate the crisp recap. Confirming acceptance of the MAP format and the asks. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- Procurement: we can issue a 30-day discovery PO to cover engineering time for VPN & test dataset ingestion. I’ll get the PO template to Claire and copy procurement@clearfin.com by EOD Monday (2027-05-17).
- Security sync: I’ll ask our infra lead (Samir Patel) to join the 05/23 slot; if he’s unavailable, Claire will propose a slot the same week.
- SOC2: legal will want a short Q&A with your security contact once the SOC2 excerpt is shared.

Two additional asks: can Redwood provide an expected cost-per-1M tokens with and without the KV cache on the pilot workload? That will be needed for CFO signoff.

I’ll confirm resources shortly. Thanks — looking forward to the VPC diagram.

John
John Lee
Head of Payments, ClearFin
john.lee@clearfin.com | (617) 555-0921

Subject: Re: Executive recap: ClearFin leadership briefing, outcomes & escalation asks

On Sun, 16 May 2027 at 15:14, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> High-level business outcomes (what ClearFin expects):
> - Reduce fraud review time for manual cases by ~60% within pilot window...
>
Thanks for the summary — noted. A couple of technical notes I want to call out for the architecture sync: 
- Regional routing: we can deploy an inference pool in their us-east region and enable Smart Routing to shift traffic to dedicated nodes in the event of saturation. That will keep p95 latency within target unless request bursts exceed burst reservation.
- KV cache: significant cost benefit for repeated token patterns in fraud scoring; I’ll include comparative numbers (cache on vs off) in the VPC diagram doc.
- Audit trail: we’ll enable per-request trace IDs and a minimal explainability payload (decision score + top-3 features) in the pilot. Need to confirm retention window with ClearFin (default 30 days).

I’ll attach the network diagram + sizing notes to the Drive link by 2027-05-23.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Lead Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Quick note from security/integration: we can support HSM/KMS integration for key rotation; will need ClearFin to confirm KMS provider (AWS KMS vs. customer HSM). For SOC2 artifacts, I can share an excerpt and a short one-pager on our processor controls by Monday.

If procurement needs a cap on spend to sign the discovery PO, we can propose a monthly commit tier with a built-in throttle to prevent cost runaway during discovery — happy to discuss numbers on the 05/17 follow-up.

—
Priyom Das
Director, Security & Integrations, Redwood Inference
